newsitem.title: UK: Burundi army massacre people in church - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army massacre people in church - Amnesty.

text.p: Burundi's Tutsi-led security forces have killed at least 1,000 unarmed Hutu civilians in the past month, attacking some of them as they sheltered in churches, Amnesty International said on Friday.
The London-based human rights organisation said that, in the latest case, up to 500 people were massacred in the Pentecostal Church of Nyarurama on December 3.

The victims had been told that they could shelter safely in the church but, once they were inside, soldiers surrounded the building, threw grenades inside and shot at or bayoneted those trying to escape, Amnesty said in a news release.
Then the troops set the church on fire, sought out those who had escaped and killed them as well.
"The local people believe that places of worship offer symbolic protection. But clearly no place appears to be too sacred for the army to carry out massacres," Amnesty said.
This was the second massacre to take place in a church in Burundi in recent weeks, Amnesty said.

"What is happening in Burundi appears to be a deliberate policy of systematic extermination of a section of the population, with (President Pierre) Buyoya presiding over more than 10,000 killings since August," Amnesty International said.
It said the army had killed at least 1,000 Hutus in four provinces since November.
Burundi was the scene of a brutal tribal conflict which broke out following the murder of Hutu President Melchior Ndadaye in 1993 and claimed 50,000 lives.
